title: Thirty-minute demo path and fallback hierarchy notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a lean, operational guide for anyone (solutions engineer, SDK PM, new hire) to run a 30-minute live demo or hands-on lab of the Redwood SDK + Hosted API and to demonstrate graceful degradation when things fail. Focus: predictable timeboxing, reproducible prompts, explicit fallback hierarchy, and telemetry hooks to observe outcome quality and cost.

Who this helps:
- Solutions engineers running customer demos
- Developer advocates doing quickstart sessions
- New PD/SDK folks rehearsing flows

High-level goals for a 30-minute slot (minutes allocation):
- 0-3m: Setup & context (credentials, brief ask)
- 3-8m: Quickstart code run (hello world generation)
- 8-15m: Show structured outputs + tool calling + streaming
- 15-22m: Failure injection and fallback walkthrough
- 22-28m: Telemetry & cost/latency breakdowns
- 28-30m: Next steps / Q&A / links

Pre-demo checklist (run 15 minutes before start):
- [ ] Confirm API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY in ephemeral shell
  - command: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-demo-xxxx
- [ ] Start local SDK quickstart runner (v0.8.3): python -m redwood_quickstart --mode demo
- [ ] Confirm model pinned in demo payload (gpt-open-1-small) and a lower-cost fallback (gpt-open-1-tiny) are available in the account
- [ ] Open Console -> Route: demo/30m -> latency & token charts
- [ ] Open a second tab to the telemetry dashboard (demo tokens / token-cost-per-minute)
- [ ] Confirm network access to hosted endpoint from demo laptop (curl test below)

Sanity curl test:
- curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health || echo "network/cred issue"

Quickstart script (5 lines — keep for live demo):
- python3 demo_apps/hello_gen.py --prompt-file examples/intro.prompt --model gpt-open-1-small --stream

Example demo prompts (use these verbatim — repeatable):
- intro.prompt:
  "You are a helpful assistant. Summarize the following product spec in three bullets and one 15-word elevator pitch. Spec:
  - single-paragraph description: Redwood makes inference predictable across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
  - target users: engineers and platform teams.
  - constraints: 100ms latency target for small requests.
  "

Structured outputs to highlight:
- JSON-schema response via function calling (show schema + runtime validation)
- Streaming partial tokens vs final output (point out latency savings)
- Embedding + rerank mini-flow (embed top-3 snippets and rerank search results)

Failure injection plan (15-22m): show graceful degradation sequence. Run each step and narrate tradeoffs.
1) Simulate transient latency spike (network throttle): 30-60s window
   - Expected behavior: SDK shows increased p99, Console alerts on latency SLOs, heuristic auto-batching reduces throughput but preserves tail latency.
   - Talking points: how KV caching and prefix caching reduce repeat-costs
2) Simulate model OOM / capacity preemption (return 500s from endpoint)
   - Fallback steps (hierarchy — execute in this order):
     a) Retry with same model with exponential backoff (2 retries, 500ms base)
     b) Route to model-variant (same architecture, lower memory quantized weight)
     c) Route to cheaper approximate model (gpt-open-1-tiny) and mark response as approximate
     d) If region-limited, route to secondary region (eu-west -> us-east) with warmed-up cache
   - Demo script: set REDWOOD_FALLBACK_POLICY=retry,variant,cheap,region
   - Show Console: annotate which fallback was used and token-delta/cost-delta
3) Simulate user error (malformed prompt causing hallucination-like output)
   - Mitigation: show prompt templates + safety checklist, automated eval against golden prompts, auto-rollout rollback if quality delta > threshold

Telemetry hooks to call out live:
- Console trace id in SDK logs (use trace header X-Redwood-Trace) and where to paste into Console search
- Token-level cost breakdown (model tokens vs user tokens) and per-route cost attribution
- Quality metric: BLEU/ROUGE snapshot against demo golden set (show simple script to run locally)
  - python demo_apps/quality_check.py --gold examples/goldset.json --out out.json

Live rollback / canary demo (one-liner to show rollouts):
- curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \ 
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts \ 
  -d '{"route":"demo/30m","candidate":"gpt-open-1-tiny","percent":20}'
- Talk through auto-fallback to previous version on metrics degradation

Narration script (short bullets to read while running flows):
- "We start with the default model to demonstrate typical quality.
- If latency spikes, the runtime tries to preserve the tail for interactive users by prioritizing p95/p99.
- If model capacity fails, our policy tries a sequence of options: quick retries, a quantized variant, then a cheaper model while labeling the response.
- Console surfaces the exact fallback used so teams can audit behavior."

Success criteria for a good demo (post-run checklist):
- [ ] Hello-gen completes in <3s for base prompt
- [ ] Fallback path executed at least once and is visible in Console trace
- [ ] Telemetry shows token breakdown and a trace id saved in notes
- [ ] Attendee(s) can reproduce quickstart with the same commands in <10 minutes

Notes to keep the demo resilient (ops tips):
- Keep a pre-seeded cache: run the same prompt 3x before demo start to warm KV cache
- Have snapshotted logs: demo_logs/<date>-traceid.txt created after pre-run
- If remote network fails, switch to recorded demo (recording link in linked_artifacts)

Open questions / TODOs (for improving this doc):
- Should we add a canned slide showing cost tradeoffs for each fallback variant? (DE-812)
- Add example customer-friendly language for when we return an approximate response (UX task)
- Should the demo default to console-only (no code) for non-technical audiences? Need decision from PD.

Appendix: quick commands reference (copyable)
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-demo-xxxx
- python3 demo_apps/hello_gen.py --prompt-file examples/intro.prompt --model gpt-open-1-small --stream
- curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- python demo_apps/chaos_injector.py --type model-oom --target demo/30m
- python demo_apps/quality_check.py --gold examples/goldset.json --out results.json

Slack references and quick links (for live help):
- #eng-devexp for live questions
- @liam (oncall for demos today)

Quick changelog:
- 2025-11-04: initial sketch, Maya

End of doc.
